An '''Advanced Proton Torpedo''' was a type of [[Proton torpedo/Legends|torpedo]] used by [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. They had a higher blast rating and exit velocity than standard [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]], though they were capable of tracking a target for less time.<ref name="SW:TF" />

During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], [[Reti]] provided [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Rhys Dallows]] with advanced proton torpedoes for use in his [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]].<ref name="SW:SF" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)}}
The [[Commander/Legends|commander]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], utilized the advanced torpedoes in his [[T-65B X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65B X-wing starfighter]]. He acquired an upgrade for his proton torpedoes during the [[Battle of Corellia (1 ABY)|Battle of Corellia]] around [[0 ABY/Legends|six]] [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the pivotal [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader}}
Skywalker also discovered the technology during the [[Ison Corridor ambush]] in the wreckage of a Rebel starship.<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike}}
Later Rogue Squadron [[Rogue Leader/Legends|leader]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] also discovered the technology in an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] during a [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|battle]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>
{{Endgame}}

[[Maarek Stele/Legends|Maarek Stele]], when often facing enemy [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defenders]] in an [[Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wing/Legends|Assault Gunboat]] or [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE Avenger]], often replaced the standard load of [[advanced concussion missile]]s with advanced proton torpedoes. While ordinary and advanced torpedoes were not designed for use against enemy starfighters, Stele used his tractor beam weapon to snare the opposing fighter, and one advanced torpedo was enough to take out a full-strength TIE Defender. This gave Stele more hitting power, as his craft could carry 6 to 12 torpedoes compared to 8 to 16 missiles.<ref name="SW:TF" />

Other Rebel forces also used the advanced proton torpedo after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].<ref name="SW:XA">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Advanced proton torpedoes first appeared in [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] as a more powerful proton torpedo. They served the same role in the later ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''. In [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']], proton torpedoes may be upgraded to the advanced version if the player picks up the upgrade during the Corellian mission. Acquiring the technology is required for the mission's gold medal, and this article assumes the player did so. The technology may also be acquired in the game's sequels, ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''.
